title: Initial evaluation, left ankle, giving way

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Hi Keisha. What happened with the left ankle?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I rolled it on an uneven trail in August, and it keeps giving way since then. Pain is 2 out of 10 today.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: How often does it give way?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Maybe once a week, usually stepping off a curb.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Let me measure. Inversion is about 25 degrees on the left, versus 35 on the right.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Single-leg balance: 8 seconds on the left, and 20 on the right.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Strength test: peroneal strength is 4/5 on the left.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I'm worried about running on the trail this fall.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: My goal is to run the trail race in October with no brace.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Assessment: the left ankle is weaker and less balanced than the right. I want to add balance work before any jumping.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Plan: balance drills twice a week, and no hopping or jumping for two weeks. Follow up in two weeks.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Should I wear a brace for walking?

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: For now, yes, on uneven ground.

expectedFacts.statement: Ankle gives way about once a week, stepping off curbs
Single-leg balance 8 seconds on the left
Goal: trail race in October with no brace
No hopping or jumping for two weeks
Brace on uneven ground for now
